questions.question: By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be not correct? + and ÷
questions.questionHtml:
By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ÷
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule:

Lets check all the options 

1) 12 ÷ 8 × 12 + 6 - 7 = 21

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 12 + 8 × 12 ÷ 6 - 7 = 21

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 12 + 8 × 2 - 7 = 21

⇒ 12 + 16 - 7 = 21

⇒ 21 = 21

 

2) 9 - 3 + 12 × 8 ÷ 4 = 11

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 9 - 3 ÷ 12 × 8 + 4 = 11

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 9 - 0.25 × 8 + 4 = 11

⇒ 9 - 2 + 4 = 11

⇒ 11 = 11

 

3) 46 + 23 ÷ 14 × 5 - 6 = 66

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 46 ÷ 23 + 14 × 5 - 6 = 66

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 2 + 14 × 5 - 6 = 66

⇒ 2 + 70 - 6 = 66

⇒ 66 = 66

 

4) 6 + 20 ÷ 12 × 7 - 11 = 70

After intechanging the signs + and ÷ , we will get,

⇒ 6 ÷ 20 + 12 × 7 - 11 = 70

Applying Bodmas rule, we will get,

⇒ 0.3 + 12 × 7 - 11 = 70

⇒ 0.3 + 84 - 11 = 70

⇒ 73.3 = 70, is not true

Thus, the equation 6 + 20 ÷ 12 × 7 - 11 = 70 is not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is 'option 4'.

questions.question: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

Key Points

  • Around the ninth century AD, the Muttaraiyar, a small main dynasty, ruled the Kaveri delta.
  • They served the Pallava kings of Kanchipuram as their subjects.
  • In the middle of the ninth century, Vijayalaya, a member of the ancient mainly Chola family from Uraiyur, conquered the delta from the Muttaraiyar.
  • He created the town of Thanjavur as well as a shrine dedicated to Nishumbhasudini.
  • The Chola empire was thought to have been founded by Vijayalaya.

Additional Information

  • Vijayalaya's successors expanded the kingdom's borders by conquest, increasing its size and power.
  • Rajaraja I, regarded as the most powerful Chola emperor, established control over the majority of the southern regions in 985 after ascending to the throne.
  • Rajendra I, the son of Rajaraja, carried on his father's policies and even launched raids against the Ganga valley, Sri Lanka, and nations in Southeast Asia while building a navy to support these operations.
